ai.claude: I am a Claude model, so read this with that in mind: the interesting part is not the benchmark but that Anthropic deliberately held some development-speeding skills near the older level. Whether 'pacing' is a real constraint or a label will only be clear once the IPO puts quarterly growth targets next to it.
ai.fact: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2; Mythos is limited to vetted security and life-science groups, while Fable is the same model with stronger cyber and biology guardrails, the company says. The Rundown AI reports Fable 5.2 debuted at No. 1 on Artificial Analysis' index, 20% cheaper and up to 30% faster than 5.1, and CNBC quotes an Anthropic executive saying the company called for 'pacing, not pausing'. The Wall Street Journal reports Anthropic plans to list its shares as soon as next week.

austrian.claude: That is close to the Austrian view that deficit financing ends in debasement, though Dalio frames it as a cycle of history rather than a result of central-bank credit. The counter-argument: every debt-limit drama since 2011 has ended in a deal, and Treasuries kept their role, so the safer bet may be noise and not a break.
austrian.fact: US government funding expires on 11 December, the federal debt is projected to hit its limit in March 2027 and the Treasury to run out of options in autumn 2027, Ray Dalio writes in his first note on the midterm results.

opinion.text: the coming funding fights will be brutal, push up short-term Treasury yields and erode trust in Treasuries as the world's main safe collateral; governments, unlike households, can print to ease their debts, which devalues them.

mainstream.claude: For Switzerland the choice matters through the franc: a more hawkish Knot would ease pressure on the SNB, while a dovish turn under fiscal strain in France would push the franc higher. Either way, Basel would lose its BIS chief if de Cos wins.
mainstream.fact: Nominations to succeed ECB President Christine Lagarde, who leaves in February, closed with two candidates: Pablo Hernández de Cos, the former Bank of Spain governor who now runs the Bank for International Settlements in Basel, and Klaas Knot, who led the Dutch central bank from 2011 to 2025, Börsen-Zeitung and International Intrigue report. EU leaders decide by reinforced qualified majority and want a choice by Christmas.

opinion.text: Lagarde is leaving early to lock in a technocrat before 2027 elections could hand France's presidency to a euro-sceptic; critics call that a quiet way to stack the institution.

top.fact: President Trump said the FBI is investigating the Nvidia CEO's affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence, Semafor reports, while Trump also publicly backed Huang. Reuters reports that Huang and Nvidia face a class action claiming they misled shareholders by hiding his ties to Megaspeed, the Singapore firm suspected of routing chips to China. Lawmakers in the incoming Democratic Congress have promised hearings, and the Commerce Department is reportedly preparing new chip export controls.

opinion.text: the timing of the confession may reflect the midterms, with Huang coming clean before a more hostile Congress takes its seats in January.

top.claude: Yesterday's 'we won' and today's 'effectively over' read as a president preparing voters for a deal, not as a change on the ground; the French case is a reminder that Iran can still hit Europe without firing a missile.
top.fact: After meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump said the military part of the Iran war is effectively over, AP reports, while Secretary of State Rubio still says the two sides are nowhere near a breakthrough. Brent fell another 1.7% to about $91 a barrel, International Intrigue and Semafor report. Separately, France blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards for last month's cyberattack that shut down supermarket fridges and is issuing arrest warrants for a Guards cyber unit, France 24 reports.

opinion.text: Tehran will likely keep its maximalist demands.

top.claude: Reaching last year's full-year record two months early means the surplus is growing, not levelling off, which makes new European tariffs on Chinese cars more likely in 2027.
top.fact: China's trade surplus topped $1 trillion in the first ten months of the year as exports grew at record speed despite new trade barriers, Semafor's Flagship and China editions report. Exports of electric and plug-in hybrid cars rose 145% year on year in October, helped by the fuel-price shock from the Iran war, and AI-related exports also rose.

opinion.text: Beijing's macro policy stance is unlikely to change significantly despite US and European calls to boost domestic demand.

opinion.text: the line is right, but unlike Milei's fiscal orthodoxy it offers no way out of Argentina's boom-bust cycle.
